body.p: Horoyin. There was a shaman. He had the name Horoyin. At that time, there was [DCh]: The use of "Énin" very bad smallpox. The smallpox ate all the people, all people died.for 'smallpox' (actually meaning 'mother') seems to be a euphemism/metaphor. Smallpox is always going. It found one pit-dwelling. In this pit-dwelling, it ate all people. It has three paths. A raven is flying here to the pit-dwelling.[DCh]: What has three paths? The pit-dwelling, or the smallpox? The raven came flying, it sat down on the pit-dwelling. Having sat down it listened. The smallpox had two children. These devils are talking. The raven is listening. The smallpox say: "I'll go along the middle way. You go along the outer paths! Let's go at night! Here is one tent nearby, let's go there! When the people will eat, let's fall into the kettle. Let's make the people eat [DCh]: The analysis of "dÊ¼awiwÉ£ot" is tentative[StN]: translation?[us]. Then let's break their bellies!" The raven hears [that]. Having heard [that] it flew off, there to the tent. It reached the tent. It sat onto the smoke hole. Then it says "alikowun, kalkowun". "Horoyin, Horoyin! Alikowun, kalkowun", the raven says. "Smallpox devils are close by!", the raven says. "I saw the smallpox devils! I heard very bad words! Horoyin, Horoyin! The smallpox devils are about to come to you this night! They are about to fall into your kettle! They are about to break your belly!" There the shaman Horoyin started to think. Having thought he says: "Saw clean(?) wood! Chop off the branches! Don't saw it into two halves! Put the wood as a whole!" And the shaman Horoyin says: "Catch four very good reindeers![DCh]: Not clear why attributive form of "oron" 'reindeer'. Kill those reindeers!" The people caught four very fat reindeer. Having caught they killed [them]. Then they sawed the wood clean (?) and put it down. How the shaman Horoyin had said, so they did. Then they cooked soup. Horoyin stood up. Having stood up he brought an iron chest. The chest has three keys. Then the shaman Horoyin sat down. Having sat down the shaman Horoyin said: "Sit closer to the kettle! Eat soup! Eat everything up!" The people sat down around the kettle. They ate one spoon of soup. Then pieces of coal fell into the kettle, into the smoke hole. Horoyin ran quickly to the kettle, then he said: "That's good! Majin has given luck!" Horoyin took that piece of coal. Then he put this piece of coal in the iron chest. Then he laid the chest on a high tree. [On] the third day in the chest a knocking was audible. [On] the seventh day, the smallpox in the chest is calling. Then the smallpox is crying. The shaman Horoyin is laughing. The smallpox is crying a lot. "Horoyin, Horoyin!", the smallpox is yelling. "Big shaman!", the smallpox says. The shaman Horoyin is laughing again. "Ha, ha, ha", he says. Again the smallpox is crying a lot. There the shaman says: "What are you crying, smallpox?" Then the smallpox says: "Big shaman, Horoyin! Release me!" The shaman Horoyin says: "How will I release you? Will you come again? Will you eat again all people? How will I release you?" There the smallpox says: "I won't go to this land anymore!" "Do you tell the truth?", the shaman says. "The truth!", the smallpox says. Then the shaman Horoyin released the smallpox.
